stepByStepInstructions: Ensure the scene is safe
Check if the person responds - shake their shoulders and shout
If no response, shout for help
Tilt their head back and lift their chin to open the airway
Check for breathing for no more than 10 seconds
If not breathing normally, start CPR immediately
Place one hand in the center of their chest, place your other hand on top
Push down hard and fast - at least 5cm deep
Do 30 chest compressions at a rate of 100-120 per minute
Give 2 rescue breaths, then continue with 30 compressions and 2 breaths
Continue until help arrives or the person starts breathing
criticalWarnings: Do not stop CPR until the person shows signs of life or help arrives
Push hard and fast - don't worry about pushing too hard
If you're not trained in rescue breaths, do continuous chest compressions only

immediateAction: Apply direct pressure to the wound immediately
stepByStepInstructions: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth or your hand
Press firmly on the wound
If cloth becomes soaked with blood, add more on top - don't remove the first cloth
If possible, elevate the injured area above the level of the heart
Keep pressure on for at least 10 minutes
If bleeding is from a limb and won't stop, consider applying a tourniquet
Keep the person still and lying down
Keep them warm with a blanket or coat
criticalWarnings: Do not remove embedded objects - stabilize them instead
Tourniquets should only be used as a last resort for life-threatening limb bleeding
Never apply a tourniquet to the neck, head, or torso

immediateAction: Encourage them to cough if they can
stepByStepInstructions: If they can cough, encourage them to keep coughing
If they cannot cough, speak, or breathe, start back blows
Stand behind them and slightly to one side
Support their chest with one hand and lean them forward
Give up to 5 sharp blows between their shoulder blades with the heel of your hand
If back blows don't work, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts
Stand behind them and put your arms around their waist
Place a clenched fist just above their belly button
Grasp the fist with your other hand and pull sharply inwards and upwards
Alternate between 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out
criticalWarnings: If they become unconscious, start CPR immediately
Don't give abdominal thrusts to babies under 1 year old
After abdominal thrusts, the person should see a doctor

immediateAction: Have them sit down and rest immediately
stepByStepInstructions: Help them sit down in a comfortable position - half sitting is best
Loosen any tight clothing around their neck and chest
Ask if they have any heart medication like GTN spray
If they have aspirin and are not allergic, have them chew one 300mg tablet
Keep them calm and reassured
Monitor their breathing and consciousness
If they have GTN spray, help them take it as prescribed
If they become unconscious and stop breathing, start CPR
criticalWarnings: Time is critical - every minute counts
Do not give aspirin if they are allergic or under 16
Do not leave them alone

stepByStepInstructions: Check for FAST signs: Face - has their face fallen on one side?
Arms - can they raise both arms and keep them there?
Speech - is their speech slurred?
Note the exact time the symptoms started - this is crucial
Lie them down with their head and shoulders slightly raised
If they're unconscious, put them in the recovery position
Do not give them anything to eat or drink
Loosen any tight clothing
Keep them calm and reassured
Monitor their breathing and consciousness
criticalWarnings: Time is critical - brain cells are dying
Even if symptoms disappear, they still need urgent assessment
Do not give aspirin - only paramedics should do this for stroke

immediateAction: Use their EpiPen/adrenaline auto-injector if they have one
stepByStepInstructions: Ask if they have an EpiPen or adrenaline auto-injector
If yes, help them use it immediately - inject into their outer thigh
Lie them down flat unless they're having trouble breathing
If they're having trouble breathing, let them sit up
If they're pregnant, lie them on their left side
If symptoms don't improve after 5 minutes, give a second injection if available
Keep them still and calm
Monitor their breathing and consciousness
criticalWarnings: They may need a second injection after 5 minutes
Remove any stinger if it's a bee sting (scrape, don't pinch)
Even if they improve, they must go to hospital

immediateAction: Protect them from injury but do not restrain them
stepByStepInstructions: Stay with them and stay calm
Protect them from injury - move furniture away
Cushion their head with something soft if possible
Time the seizure if you can
Do not restrain them or put anything in their mouth
After the seizure, put them in the recovery position
Stay with them until they are fully recovered
They may be confused or sleepy afterwards - this is normal
criticalWarnings: Call 999 if it's their first seizure, lasts more than 5 minutes, or they have multiple seizures
Never put anything in their mouth during a seizure
Do not give them water or food until fully conscious

immediateAction: Cool the burn with cool running water for at least 20 minutes
stepByStepInstructions: Remove the person from the heat source
Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes
Remove any clothing or jewelry near the burn unless stuck to the skin
Keep cooling while waiting for help
Cover the burn with cling film or a clean plastic bag
Do not use ice, creams, or ointments
Keep the person warm with a blanket, avoiding the burned area
Monitor their breathing and consciousness
criticalWarnings: Do not use ice - it can cause more damage
Do not burst any blisters
Large burns or burns to the face, hands, or genitals need urgent medical attention
